idiom_name: Django REST framework renderer classes (TemplateHTMLRenderer + JSONRenderer)
implementation_notes: The presentation is modelled as a list of renderer classes: renderer_classes = [TemplateHTMLRenderer, JSONRenderer, BrowsableAPIRenderer] is content-negotiated from the Accept header (or a format suffix) and the same serialized data is handed to the selected renderer, so a single endpoint returns HTML pages and API payloads - the renderer list replaces the classic view registry. Plain Django is the lightweight variant: compute the model once in the view and return render(request, 'movie.html', context) for HTML and JsonResponse(data) for JSON, with one shared serializer so the two cannot diverge. Keep the classic attached-observer structure only for push-style presentations (notification of several live observers), which Django's request/response cycle does not provide.
pitfalls: TemplateHTMLRenderer expects Response.data to be a dict: passing serializer output straight through renders a list into the template context and fails at a confusing point.
Each renderer re-walks the data, so an unoptimized HTML renderer beside a JSON one is the usual source of N+1 queries (select_related/prefetch_related must serve both).
Format-suffix negotiation (format='json' in the URL) bypasses the Accept header and confuses caches and proxies; keep negotiation header-driven and pin media_type on custom renderers.
